<main>

## Introduction

This report shows the features available in the RAP Skeleton Lite. The RAP
Skeleton Lite is used to create simple HTML reports. It can also convert
Microsoft Word documents into HTML reports.

`r f_borderline()`

## CSS file for NISRA branding

The `style.css` file is in the project's code folder.
It controls how this report looks, including colours, fonts and page layout.
The file follows NISRA and departmental branding guidance. It also follows
accessibility guidance to help make the report easy to use.

Changes to the visual presentation of the document can be made by editing the
`style.css` file. More information on how to write CSS code can be found
[on the W3 schools website](https://www.w3schools.com/css/default.asp).

`r f_borderline()`

## NISRA banner

The banner, which can be seen at the very top of this document, is called using
the function:

```
`f_banner(title = "RAP Skeleton Lite Demo")`
```

This can be configured in the `config.R` script by changing the
value of `nics_theme`:

```
nics_theme <- "dof"
```

`nics_theme` accepts any of the following values: "teo", "daera", "dfc", "de",
"dfe", "dof", "dfi", "doh", "doj", "bso", "adr". Setting nics_theme to your
department will automatically update the relevant colours, logos, alt texts and
departmental links contained in the banner (and throughout the rest of the
document).

The title and subtitle can be defined when calling the function:

```
f_banner(title = "Rap Skeleton Lite Demo", subtitle = "Optional Subtitle")
```

`r f_borderline()`

## Definition boxes

If you would like to highlight a particular piece of text, such as a definition
or block quote you can use the function:

```
f_definition_box(
  "The function for a definition box is defined in the Functions.R file and can
  be called using this function"
)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
f_definition_box(
  "The function for a definition box is defined in the Functions.R file and can
  be called using this function"
)
```

`r f_borderline()`

## Custom boxes

You can enhance the presentation of your reports by writing HTML and CSS in your
document. One way to do this is by using div boxes to highlight specific data or
information, as shown in the example below.

```
<div class="container">
  <div class="box">
      <div>Population registered with a health service dentist</div>
      <div class="value">70%</div>
  </div>
  <div class="box">
      <div>Pupils enrolled in pre-school education, 2022</div>
      <div class="value">22,558</div>
  </div>
```
```
<!--html_preserve-->
<div class="container">
  <div class="box">
      <div>Population registered with a health service dentist</div>
      <div class="value">70%</div>
  </div>
  <div class="box">
      <div>Pupils enrolled in pre-school education, 2022</div>
      <div class="value">22,558</div>
  </div>
<!--/html_preserve-->
```

How it works:

*	HTML structure: The code uses standard HTML for creating a grid of boxes. Each
box contains a title and a value, which can be customized based on your content.

*	CSS for styling: CSS has been added to `style.css` and is used to control the
layout, colours, spacing, and overall appearance of the boxes.

`r f_borderline()`

## Images

The NISRA logo as well as logos for all departments are found in the project
folder: `(.../rap-skeleton-lite/images/)`. You should save any images you use in
this folder.

Call an image in your rmd file (ensuring your file path uses forward slashes)
using:

```         
{r image, fig.alt="text description of image"}

knitr::include_graphics("../example/example.png")
```
For example:

```         
{r image, fig.alt="NISRA logo"}

knitr::include_graphics("../images/NISRA_logo_bilingual_colour.png")
```

```{r image,fig.alt="NISRA logo"}
knitr::include_graphics("../images/NISRA_logo_bilingual_colour.png")
```

Alt text is required for images. If the image is for decoration, use fig.alt=""
so that a screenreader will ignore it. Otherwise, include a short description of
the image using fig.alt = "description". 

Alternatively, for more control over the display of your image you can use
HTML. This approach is useful if you need to change how images are
shown (e.g. setting width, height and alignment). Learn more about adding
images using HTML
[on the W3 schools website.](https://www.w3schools.com/html/html_images.asp#:~:text=The%20HTML%20%3Cimg%3E%20tag%20is%20used)

`r f_borderline()`

## Tables

This section includes a number of basic tables. It is recommended that only
small demonstration tables should be included in the document.

Demonstration tables are small tables which highlight important messages clearly
and include commentary.

To make tables easy for everyone to use, give each column a clear heading in one
header row. Also remember these tips:

-   do not merge cells
-   do not have blank rows or columns
-   every column should have a heading
-   make sure all headings and labels are visible
-   use consistent rounding
-   left align text, or row labels, right align numbers
-   use thousand comma separator
-   avoid abbreviations or make sure they are explained clearly
-   use a caption for table titles
-   put any data labels in the headings such as % or millions or STG
-   do not use symbols such as \* or superscripts to create notes or
explanations, use [note x]

### Table 1

The following code displays a table using the Kable package. More help with
kable can be found in the
[Rmarkdown cookbook](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/kable.html).

```{r, echo=TRUE, class.source = 'fold-hide', message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
data.frame(
  Option_A = c(
    paste0(
      "Single (never married or never legally registered ",
      "a civil partnership) "
    ),
    "Married or in a legally registered civil partnership",
    paste0(
      "Separated (but still legally married or still legally ",
      "in a civil partnership)"
    ),
    paste0(
      "Divorced or formerly in a civil partnership which is ",
      "now legally dissolved"
    ),
    paste0(
      "Widowed or surviving member of a legally registered ",
      "civil partnership"
    ),
    "No code required (for under 16s)"
  ),
  Option_B = c(
    "1",
    "2",
    "3",
    "4",
    "5",
    "6"
  )
) |>
  select(
    "Option A" = Option_A,
    "Option B" = Option_B
  ) |>
  kbl(
    escape = FALSE,
    align = "lr"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(
    full_width = TRUE
  )
```

### Table 2 (pagination)

Pagination means breaking information into different pages and letting people
move between them. For longer tables, you may want to use pagination. The
following table is created using the DT package.
[More help with the DT package can be found here](https://rstudio.github.io/DT/).

```{r, echo=TRUE, class.source = 'fold-hide', warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
datatable(
  df_mye_year_gender_t,
  # DT creates row numbers by default. Suppress to ensure all cols have a header
  rownames = FALSE,
  # Rename column headers to make them descriptive
  colnames = c(
    "Mid Year Ending",
    "Females",
    "Males",
    "NI Population Total"
  ),
  caption = paste0(
    "Number of males and females making up the total NI population from ",
    earliest_year,
    "-",
    latest_year
  ),
  # Left align first column and add thousand separators to numbers.
  options = list(
    columnDefs = list(
      list(
        className = "dt-left",
        targets = 0
      )
    )
  )
) |>
  formatRound(
    c(
      "Females",
      "Males",
      "All persons"
    ),
    digits = 0,
    interval = 3,
    mark = ","
  )
```

## Hyperlinks

Use words for links that tell people where the link goes. For example,
[NISRA](www.nisra.gov.uk) rather than https://www.nisra.gov.uk/.  

When writing link text:

* use words that tells people where the link goes
* do not use link text like "click here" or "read more"
* if a link downloads a file, say what type of file it is and how big it is 
* links should open in the same window
* add “(opens in a new window)” to links that open a new window

Add a hyperlink using:

```         
[Text to display](URL path)
```

Example:

```         
[GSS harmonisation standards and guidance](https://analysisfunction.civilservice.gov.uk/government-statistical-service-and-statistician-group/gss-support/gss-harmonisation-support/harmonised-standards-and-guidance/)
```

`r f_borderline()`

## Table of contents

### Header tags (h3)

Use headings to organise your document. People who use screen readers use
headings to move around a document. Use the correct heading style for each
heading. The heading colour is #1460aa because it is easier to see and meets
accessibility standards.

When using headings:

*	use Heading 1 only for the document title
*	do not use Heading 1 anywhere else
*	do not use headings just to make text stand out
*	do not use bold text, colours, or bigger text instead of headings
*	use headings in order: Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 3, then Heading 4
*	do not miss out a heading level

More detailed guidance on writing for web is available in the Drupal user manual
published by Dissemination Branch. You can find the
[Drupal user manual](https://nicsonline.sharepoint.com/sites/TM-DOF-NISRATEAM/SitePages/DISSEMINATION%20NISRA-Website.aspx?ct=1727952358098&or=Teams-HL&ga=1&LOF=1)
and [other accessibility guidance](https://nicsonline.sharepoint.com/sites/TM-DOF-NISRATEAM/SitePages/DISSEMINATION%20Accessibility.aspx?ct=1727952463891&or=Teams-HL&ga=1&LOF=1)
on NISRA Teams Channel.

The code below shows code written in yml. This code sets up the table of
contents (toc).

```         
html_document:
  toc: true
  toc_float: true
  toc_depth: 4
```
Please see below for the different settings which can be changed to alter the
structure of your HTML document:

* toc – can be true or false, this determines whether the table of contents is
visible
* toc_float – can be true or false, this determines whether the table of
contents appears at the top of page or at the side
* toc_depth – enter a number, determines the level of nested headings which
appear in the table of contents

Headings and sub headings are then defined and registered in the table of
contents using hash keys:

```
## Heading

### Subheading
```

### Example subheading

`r f_borderline()`

## Lists

Unordered lists can be created using \*, + and - symbols:

```         
* Item 1
* Item 2
    + Item 2a
        - Item 2a.a
        - Item 2a.b
    + Item 2b
* Item 3
    + Item 3a
```

Output:

-   Item 1
-   Item 2
    -   Item 2a
        -   Item 2a.a
        -   Item 2a.b
    -   Item 2b
-   Item 3
    -   Item 3a

Ordered lists can be created using numbers followed by the contents with a space
in between. Similar to unordered lists, you can add extra layers as needed:

```         
1. Item 1
2. Item 2
3. Item 3
    + Item 3a
    + Item 3b
```

output:

1. Item 1
2. Item 2
3. Item 3
    + Item 3a
    + Item 3b

`r f_borderline()`

```{js}

// Function to add tabs to table of contents

function tabOrder() {

  // Make side menu tabbable

  let headings = document.getElementsByClassName(
    "tocify-item list-group-item"
  );

  let sections = document.getElementsByClassName(
    "section"
  );

  for (let i = 0; i < headings.length; i++) {
    headings[i].innerHTML =
      "<a href='#" +
      sections[i].id +
      "'>" +
      headings[i].innerHTML +
      "</a>";
  }
}

// Instruct web browser to run above function when loaded
window.onload = tabOrder;
```
